# Eric W. Tramel

> Personal site of Eric W. Tramel, Ph.D. — Principal Research Scientist at NVIDIA. Research in synthetic data generation, federated learning, and the intersection of statistical physics and machine learning.

Eric's site includes a blog on ML engineering and agent tooling, a full academic publication list, and a professional bio.

## Blog

- [Slop Guard: Prose Linter for AI-Assisted Writing](https://eric-tramel.github.io/blog/2026-02-18-slop-guard.md): A rule-based prose linter that catches formulaic writing patterns LLMs fall into. No LLM judge, no API calls. Just compiled regex and an afternoon of calibration against human reference texts.
- [Why Not Both?](https://eric-tramel.github.io/blog/2026-02-09-why-not-both.md): Wiring OpenAI's Codex into Claude Code via MCP. Two model families, one terminal, real bugs found.
- [Searchable Agent Memory in a Single File](https://eric-tramel.github.io/blog/2026-02-07-searchable-agent-memory.md): A single-file BM25 MCP server that gives a Claude Code agent searchable access to its own conversation history.
- [CUDA Perceptron in 2008](https://eric-tramel.github.io/blog/2025-08-21-cuda-perceptron-in-2008.md): After I finished by B.S. in Computer Engineering, my thought was to take a quick two year extension into a Masters degree, just for pure marketability
- [Compressive Lightfield Imaging](https://eric-tramel.github.io/blog/2025-08-20-compressive-lightfield-imaging.md): This patent resulted from the most fun two weeks of work I had during my summer internship at Canon. I had joined principally to work on optimization
- [Site Refresh, 2019](https://eric-tramel.github.io/blog/2019-12-26-site-refresh.md): Refreshing the personal site after a few years.
- [Nothing to Julia in Minutes](https://eric-tramel.github.io/blog/2016-03-06-nothing-to-julia.md): Starting up with Julia for the first time.
- [Building SPAMS](https://eric-tramel.github.io/blog/2014-04-07-building-spams.md): Building the SPAMS Matlab package for sparse modelling.
